regions.name: flow_near_wake
regions.why: Create the missing off-body near-wake box so the separated-shear-layer / bluff-body wake envelope is covered. Bounds are the flow_requirement:near_wake envelope padded by ~0.01 m so the float32 bounds (0.3499999940/1.0499999821/+-0.9799999833/+-0.4899999917) are strictly contained. Level 2 gives 0.04375 m, half the 0.0875 m prior (= exactly level 1), leaving a factor-2 margin for the native p95 span statistic (tolerance 1.5) instead of a knife-edge equality. Level 2 stays coarser than surface level 3, so no surface/layer/quality setting changes and the surface -> wake -> background grading is preserved. Volume 0.72*1.98*1.00 = 1.43 m^3, ~1.7e4 cells. This is an envelope prior, not a measured shear-layer thickness.

regions.name: flow_far_wake
regions.why: Cover the downstream velocity-deficit/shear transport envelope, padded ~0.01-0.02 m beyond the float32 bounds (1.0499999821/2.4499999583/+-1.2599999785/+-0.6299999893). The prior span 0.175 m is EXACTLY the uniform background cell (grading 1.0), so leaving it unboxed relies on an equality that any stricter native comparison or transition cell would break; level 1 = 0.0875 m supplies a factor-2 margin at ~6.9e3 cells. The upstream face overlaps the near-wake box by 0.02 m so maximum level wins and no coarse slot appears between the two envelopes. Kept deliberately at one increment (the scenario states coarser far-wake bounds cost), not refined to surface level.

regions.name: repair_0
regions.why: actual layer deficit concentrated in measured boundary faces

advisor.hypothesis: The two acceptance reasons are separate defects. (1) Layer coverage: 0.682 with 22.1% of body area at ZERO layers and 0.657 at 6 layers; the zero-layer band (layer_shortfall:0 y=0.564..0.744, layer_shortfall:1 y=-0.744..-0.564, both spanning x/z=+-0.393) is exactly the two streamwise end caps, which are geometrically DISJOINT from the barrel annulus in the body bounding box (the barrel is the axis-parallel surface |y|<=0.70 at r=0.35; the caps are the normal-to-y discs at |y|=0.70). A cylinder wall patch discretizes to isolated `body` polygon patches per face and each cyl cap is a multi-patch disc: snappy extrudes per patch, so the axis-normal patch rim has no coherent normal direction and extrusion cells at the rim cross the solid. So a polygon-level medial-axis claim is NOT justified here: the native FLUID medial distance at the cap rim is small and the cap patches have no usable normal, and the observed 0-layer fraction is the shrinker's own budget refusing those faces (it removes non-positive layers), not an angle clamp. Raising feature_angle 60->120 to bypass the crease does nothing because the deficit is 0 layers (not 1-4) and the medial-shrinker collapse mechanism is unchanged; it ALSO caused the round-2 regression (0.840->0.682) by killing the smooth barrel. (2) The failed native self-intersection check is a transition/snap-fold artifact at the rim, evidenced by the transition and snap_artifact clusters sitting at wall distance 0.03-0.09 m around the rim. (3) Off-body resolution is already acceptable: native near-wake p95 0.0457 m vs prior 0.0875 (0.52x) and far-wake 0.0911 vs 0.175 (0.52x), both accepted; surface/distances boxes must be preserved. The mechanism NOT yet tried in any round: seed extra medial layer space at the rim by adding a thin distance-level insert near the body that resolves the cap rim BEFORE the layers stage (feature refinement), instead of refining the snapped VOLUME (local_refine to level 4, round 1), which added cells without creating layer space. Combine that with the shrinker's own corner mechanisms (min_medial_axis_angle down from 90 to 60, thickness smoothing to 30, n_buffer_cells_no_extrude 0) while restoring the round-0 angle/expansion settings.
advisor.expected_change: Area fraction with >=5 actual layers should rise from 0.682 toward the >=0.90 gate (target >=0.90) and the 0-layer area fraction should fall from 0.221 toward <0.05, because the rim gains local medial space before the layer stage and the shrinker's own corner budget stops refusing the cap faces. Native near-wake p95 axis span stays ~0.046 m (<=0.0875) and far-wake ~0.091 m (<=0.175); cells grow modestly above 170k. Uncertainty: whether v2412 snappyLayerDriver honours the medial-angle override (its own corner layer insertion uses a similar threshold less the 30 deg deduction, so lowering to 60 should admit more corner points); if not, coverage improvement will be smaller than predicted and the thin rim inserts are the fallback. The self-intersection check is expected to clear or improve because re-enabled medial smoothing plus the finer rim face reduces the snap fold; this is not certified by any current measurement.
alternatives: If coverage stalls below 0.90, drop feature_angle back to 60 but keep expansion_ratio 1.1 (round 1 settings) and instead move the cap-rim space from the caps to the barrel: raise only the rounded shoulder/anchor location with a second thin distance-level insert at 0.06 m, level 3.

If the medial-angle override is rejected in v2412, switch mesh_shrinker to displacementMotionSolver (relative size 0.4, diffusivity quadratic inverseDistance) which smooths the shrinking; the torus ablation warns motion-solver alone left 1.74% coverage, so this must be combined with active thickness smoothing and accepted only if native coverage and quality both pass.

If the self-intersection failure persists with acceptable layer coverage, keep the state (fidelity and quality gates already pass at all three anchors) and treat the artifact as a native surfaceCheck observation, but that is NOT acceptance and must be stated as such.
counterevidence: feature_angle 60 with 8 layers and expansion 1.2 gave the BEST coverage (0.797) and max_skew 0.51, so widening the angle is not generally the answer.
feature_angle 120 with 6 layers and expansion 1.1 REGRESSED coverage to 0.682 and left 22.1% of area at 0 layers, i.e. it did not simply bypass a 90 deg crease suppression.

Round 1 local_refine to level 4 at the rim raised cells 187k->256k, coverage only 0.797->0.841, and max_skew 0.51->2.85: refining the snapped VOLUME does not create medial layer space, so cell count is explicitly not the mechanism.

All three anchors report native_polygon_closed/oriented true and native_failure_messages empty, so the failed self-intersection check is not a global geometry decomposition failure and the sampled fidelity 6.9e-3 m tolerance already passes.
no measured flow/probe data exists, so no wall_shear/y+ driven first-height change is permitted; first layer height must remain the physical 0.0010702 m.
the scenario states off-body boxes are unvalidated hypotheses; they nonetheless already pass with 1.5x margin, so they are preserved unchanged rather than re-optimised.
if the n_buffer_cells_no_extrude override is not honoured, zeroing adjacent displacement may reduce the covered area near the rim and partially offset the gain.

actions.why: No plan is eligible_for_restore (all three provisional), so the anchor must be referenced by its measured ID per the reference. Round 0 is the highest-coverage measured anchor (0.797) with the best quality (max_non_ortho 42.0, max_skew 0.51, min_volume 2.5e-7) and its native near/far-wake spans pass; per instructions an ineligible anchor is restored as the SPEC BASELINE for its layer_parameters (n_surface_layers 8, expansion_ratio 1.2, feature_angle 60, min_medial_axis_angle 90, n_smooth_thickness 10, n_smooth_normals 3, n_smooth_surface_normals 1, n_buffer_cells_no_extrude 0) rather than copied verbatim.

actions.name: rim_shoulder
actions.why: Feature (geometry+surface-resolution) refinement, not layer patching: replace the round-1 repair_0 level-4 band with a level-3 insert that forces 0.04375/2 = 0.021875 m cells over the shoulder band |y| in 0.70..0.90. This creates feature space and sharper native faces at the cap rim before snapping so the cutter resolves the rim instead of folding snapped faces into itself, and gives the layer stage more local medial cell budget. Written as update_region because the restored round-0 spec already contains the flow_near_wake/flow_far_wake boxes (this is the same mechanic round 1 used for its level-2 slot); level 3 equals the surface level, inside the +2 bound, and preserves both declared wake envelopes (wake cells 0.04375 m, so 0.021875/0.04375 = 0.5x the near-wake prior, unchanged).

Corner/medial-space treatment aimed at the measured ZERO-layer band (22.1% of area) and the failed native self-intersection: re-enable a thin near-body refinement only through distance_levels (level 2 at 0.05 m vs prior 0.13125 m) so the rim face is resolved enough for a valid snap, then relax the shrinker's own corner gates so the cap patches extrude instead of refusing: min_medial_axis_angle 90 -> 60 (the shrinker's corner-point insertion excludes 'angle to nearest layer patch > minMedialAxisAngle - 30 deg', i.e. 60 deg admits points it previously rejected), n_smooth_thickness 20 and n_smooth_normals 8 and n_relax_iter 8 to redistribute the rim displacement, while restoring round 0's proven angle/expansion pair (feature_angle 60, expansion_ratio 1.2) that gave the best measured coverage; expansion_ratio 1.1 is a correction since it is not allowed as a separate action and its stack effect (0.0177 -> 0.0161 m) is far below the medial distance. min_medial_axis_angle and n_smooth_thickness are written explicitly because the restored anchor's values (90, 10) would otherwise cancel the mechanism.

The failed native self-intersection check is a seam/rim snap fold (transition + snap_artifact clusters at 0.03-0.09 m wall distance around the rim), so give the snapper more budget to converge on a single-valued rim instead of folding: n_solve_iter 40->100, n_feature_snap_iter 10->24, n_relax_iter 5->12, n_smooth_patch 3->8, keeping explicit (implicit false) snapping and tolerance 2.0 so no additional insertion-scale change is introduced at this stage. This does not loosen any quality/fidelity gate and is the only lever that can plausibly clear the self-intersection observation without coarsening the geometry.
